From 3dd4d40b420846dd35869ccc8f8627feef2cff32 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Date: Wed, 23 Oct 2019 17:00:45 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] xfs: Sanity check flags of Q_XQUOTARM call

Flags passed to Q_XQUOTARM were not sanity checked for invalid values.
Fix that.

Fixes: 9da93f9b7cdf ("xfs: fix Q_XQUOTARM ioctl")
Reported-by: Yang Xu <xuyang2018.jy@cn.fujitsu.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Reviewed-by: Eric Sandeen <sandeen@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>

diff --git a/fs/xfs/xfs_quotaops.c b/fs/xfs/xfs_quotaops.c
index cd6c7210a373..c7de17deeae6 100644
--- a/fs/xfs/xfs_quotaops.c
+++ b/fs/xfs/xfs_quotaops.c
@@ -201,6 +201,9 @@ xfs_fs_rm_xquota(
 	if (XFS_IS_QUOTA_ON(mp))
 		return -EINVAL;
 
+	if (uflags & ~(FS_USER_QUOTA | FS_GROUP_QUOTA | FS_PROJ_QUOTA))
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	if (uflags & FS_USER_QUOTA)
 		flags |= XFS_DQ_USER;
 	if (uflags & FS_GROUP_QUOTA)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `fs/xfs/xfs_quotaops.c`**
- Added a sanity check for the `uflags` variable to ensure that it does not contain any invalid flags. Specifically, it checks if `uflags` has any bits set that are not part of the valid flags (`FS_USER_QUOTA`, `FS_GROUP_QUOTA`, `FS_PROJ_QUOTA`). If invalid flags are detected, the function returns `-EINVAL`.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug related to the `Q_XQUOTARM` ioctl call, which previously did not validate the flags passed to it. By implementing this sanity check, the patch ensures that only valid flags are processed, thereby preventing potential errors or undefined behavior that could arise from invalid flag values. This change is a direct fix for the issue reported in the previous commit identified by the hash `9da93f9b7cdf`.

Here is the commit message:
xfs: Sanity check flags of Q_XQUOTARM call

Flags passed to Q_XQUOTARM were not sanity checked for invalid values.
Fix that.

Fixes: 9da93f9b7cdf ("xfs: fix Q_XQUOTARM ioctl")
Reported-by: Yang Xu <xuyang2018.jy@cn.fujitsu.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Reviewed-by: Eric Sandeen <sandeen@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <darrick.wong@oracle.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the lack of validation for the flags passed to the `Q_XQUOTARM` ioctl call, allowing invalid flag values to be processed, which could lead to errors or undefined behavior in the quota management functionality.

Here is the patch:
 
 STATIC int
 xfs_fs_rm_xquota(
 	struct super_block	*sb,
 	unsigned int		uflags)
 {
 	struct xfs_mount	*mp = XFS_M(sb);
 	unsigned int		flags = 0;
 
 	if (sb_rdonly(sb))
 		return -EROFS;
 
 	if (XFS_IS_QUOTA_ON(mp))
 		return -EINVAL;
 
+	if (uflags & ~(FS_USER_QUOTA | FS_GROUP_QUOTA | FS_PROJ_QUOTA))
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	if (uflags & FS_USER_QUOTA)
 		flags |= XFS_DQ_USER;
 	if (uflags & FS_GROUP_QUOTA)
 		flags |= XFS_DQ_GROUP;
 	if (uflags & FS_PROJ_QUOTA)
 		flags |= XFS_DQ_PROJ;
 
 	return xfs_qm_scall_trunc_qfiles(mp, flags);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (uflags & ~(FS_USER_QUOTA | FS_GROUP_QUOTA | FS_PROJ_QUOTA))
```
Reason:
The code checks if any invalid flag bits are set, but if such bits are present, the function proceeds without returning a meaningful error, leading to invalid values being processed, which could result in errors or undefined behavior in the quota management functionality.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+	if (uflags & ~(FS_USER_QUOTA | FS_GROUP_QUOTA | FS_PROJ_QUOTA))
+		return -EINVAL;
```
Reason:
This addition performs a sanity check on the flags passed to the `Q_XQUOTARM` ioctl call, ensuring that only valid flag values are accepted. If invalid values are detected, it returns `-EINVAL`, effectively preventing the function from proceeding with erroneous states.
